# FEAT-000 — Feature name

**Status:** Draft / Accepted / Superseded
**Sequence:** NNNN; create `NNNN-short-name.md` and register it in the specification index. Supporting documents share the prefix. Follow the naming/delivery rules in `docs/README.md`; do not infer implementation order from a Draft number.
**Updated:** YYYY-MM-DD
**Acceptance decision:** Maintainer request/date or decision reference; do not invent acceptance.
**Backlog:** Item identifier and link when instantiated.

## User outcome and motivation

Who is in what situation, what can they accomplish, and what shows it helped?

## Scope and non-goals

State the smallest useful behavior and excluded adjacent work.

## Behavior and interaction

Inputs, validation, outputs, states and valid transitions. Describe loading/empty/error/recovery behavior, keyboard/focus and responsive behavior as applicable. Avoid prescribing code structure unless it is part of the contract.

## Acceptance and evidence

| ID   | Observable outcome    | Verification method / test           | Result/evidence |
| ---- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------ | --------------- |
| AC-1 | Given … when … then … | Unit / integration / browser / human | Pending         |

Include relevant failure and accessibility cases. Name the real browser/device/fixture needed for claims automation cannot establish.

## Data, privacy, security, compatibility

Stored/transmitted data, permissions, supported platforms, resource cleanup, schema/migration and deletion behavior. Use “not applicable, because …” rather than inventing features to fill headings.

## Dependencies and decisions

Related specs, consequential ADRs, what earlier behavior is replaced, and rollout/rollback implications.

## Open questions

List blockers to acceptance and a way to resolve each. An accepted spec must not leave material behavior undecided.
